'''Sri Niwas''' (1946–2012) was an Indian [[geophysicist]] and a professor at the Department of Earth Sciences of the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Roorkee]].<ref name="Professors - Department of Earth Sciences">{{Cite web |url=http://rurkiu.tripod.com/acd-earth/fac.html |title=Professors - Department of Earth Sciences |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Institute of Technology, Roorkee}}</ref><ref name="Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Awardees">{{Cite web |url=http://rurkiu.tripod.com/uor/handa.html |title=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Awardees |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Institute of Technology, Roorkee}}</ref> He was known for his researches on the ''Inversion of Geophysical Data''.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=89 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2016 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> He was an elected fellow of all the three major Indian science academies viz. [[Indian National Science Academy]],<ref name="List of fellows">{{Cite web |url=https://www.academia.edu/1162235 |title=List of fellows |date=2016 |publisher=Academia}}</ref> [[Indian Academy of Sciences]],<ref name="Fellow profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Sri_Niwas,_Prof._ |title=Fellow profile |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> [[National Academy of Sciences, India]]<ref name="NASI fellows">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/Year%20Book%202015.pdf |title=NASI fellows |date=2016 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India}}</ref> as well as [[Indian Geophysical Union]]<ref name="IGU fellows">{{Cite web |url=http://www.igu.in/igu_directory.pdf |title=IGU fellows |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Geophysical Union}}</ref> and was an elected member of the Association of Exploration Geophysicists.<ref name="Members List">{{Cite web |url=http://www.aegind.org/Members.html |title=Members List |date=2016 |publisher=Association of Exploration Geophysicists}}</ref> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards for his contributions to Earth, Atmosphere, Ocean and Planetary Sciences in 1991.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | accessdate=12 November 2016}}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Long link - please select award year to see details}}

== Biography ==
[[File:Admin Block IIT-R.JPG|thumb|235px|left|Indian Institute of Technology, Roorkee]]
Sri Niwas, born on 4 July 1946 in Rakhat village of [[Gorakhpur district]], in the Indian state of [[Uttar Pradesh]] to Ram Adhar Pandey, did his early schooling at local schools to complete his intermediate course from [[Board of High School and Intermediate Education Uttar Pradesh]] before joining [[Banaras Hindu University]] for his college education from where he passed BSc hons degree in 1966 and MSc in geophysics in 1968.<ref name="Faculty profile">{{Cite web |url=http://people.iitr.ernet.in/facultyresume/srsnpfes.pdf |title=Faculty profile |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Institute of Technology, Roorkee}}</ref> He enrolled for doctoral studies at the same university and secured a PhD in 1974 for his thesis, ''Theoretical treatment of some problems on electrical behavior of layered Earth system''.<ref name="Sri Niwas (1946–2012)">{{Cite journal |last=R. N. Singh, S. S. Rai |title=Sri Niwas (1946–2012) |url=http://www.currentscience.ac.in/Volumes/104/03/0373.pdf |journal=Current Science |publication-date=February 2013 |volume=104 |issue=3 |pages=373–374}}</ref> Subsequently, he did his post-doctoral studies at the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Roorkee]] (then known as University of Roorkee) and in 1976, joined the institution as a pool officer to start his career. He served out his entire career at IIT Roorkee, holding such positions as a Lecturer (1977–79) and Reader (1980–91) before superannuating in 2011 as a professor. In between, he served as a professor, chair of the Department of Geophysics and joint director of the Summer School<ref name="Summer School">{{Cite web |url=http://www.geosocindia.org/index.php/jgsi/article/download/66553/52112 |title=Summer School |date=2016 |publisher=Geological Society of India}}</ref> of [[Kurukshetra University]] from 1989 to 1992 on deputation and as a visiting professor at [[Federal University of Bahia]] during 2000–01. Post-retirement, he continued his association with IIT Roorkee as an emeritus professor.<ref name="Sri Niwas (1946–2012)" />

Sri Niwas was married to Shashi Kala and the couple had three children. He died on 15 November 2012, at the age 67.<ref name="Sri Niwas (1946–2012)" />

== Legacy ==
The researches of Niwas were focused on the geophysical problems with regard to their forward and inverse solutions and his pioneering work assisted in the electrical exploration of groundwater in alluvial terrains.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=1999}}</ref> He proposed models of system matrix function in terms of exponential functions and designed a methodology using singular value decomposition which is reported to have applications in a variety of geological environments.<ref name="Sri Niwas (1946–2012)" /> His studies have been detailed in several peer-reviewed articles;{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography'' section}} the online article repository of the Indian Academy of Sciences has listed a number of them.<ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Sri_Niwas=3AProf=2E=3A=3A.html |title=Browse by Fellow |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> He also guided 12 doctoral and 110 MTech students in their studies.<ref name="Sri Niwas (1946–2012)" /> His contributions were reported in the establishment of the Department of Geophysics at Kurukshetra University and he was one of the group of academicians who designed a curriculum in geophysics for IIT Roorkee. He was a life member of the Indian Geological Congress<ref name="Life Member">{{Cite web |url=http://igcroorkee.net/preview/pages/GBM%20Biennial%20Reprot.pdf |title=Life Member |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Geological Congress}}</ref> and a member of the faculty of Earth Sciences of the ''Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research'' (INSPIRE) program of the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]].<ref name="INSPIRE Members">{{Cite web |url=http://www.inspire-dst.gov.in/List_of_Chairpersons_Members.pdf |title=INSPIRE Members |date=2016 |publisher=Department of Science and Technology}}</ref> He was also involved with the Summer School program of the [[Science and Engineering Research Council]] (SERC)<ref name="Summer School" /> and was a referee of ''Proceedings in Earth and Planetary Sciences'' of the Indian Academy of Sciences.<ref name="A Debt of Gratitude">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/article/fulltext/jess/109/04/0549-0551 |title=A Debt of Gratitude |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1991.<ref name="Earth Sciences">{{Cite web |url=http://www.csir.res.in/External/Heads/career/award/BPRIZE/Earth_SCIENCES.htm |title=Earth Sciences |date=2016 |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303200915/http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/career/award/BPRIZE/Earth_SCIENCES.htm |archivedate=3 March 2016 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> He was an elected fellow of the Indian National Science Academy, Indian Academy of Sciences, National Academy of Sciences, India and the Indian Geophysical Union<ref name="Sri Niwas (1946–2012)" /> and a member of the Association of Exploration Geophysicists.<ref name="Members List" />
